rows.text: **Sodium carbonate** — anhydrous soda ash (mp 851 °C) or efflorescent decahydrate washing soda (Na₂CO₃·10H₂O → Na₂CO₃·H₂O in air) — is a **mild base by hydrolysis**: CO₃²⁻ + H₂O ⇌ HCO₃⁻ + OH⁻ gives pH ≈ 11, while bicarbonate sits at 8.3.…

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "An aqueous solution of sodium carbonate is alkaline due to the hydrolysis of the carbonate ion, although the salt itself contains no hydroxide."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The kettle's white scale, undone*** — permanent hardness boiled into CaSO₄ scale yields to washing soda: Na₂CO₃ + CaSO₄ → CaCO₃↓ + Na₂SO₄ — the carbonate swaps partners and the calcium leaves as a soft, removable precipitate.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Washing Soda and Its Reactions Sodium carbonate exists anhydrous (soda ash) and as the decahydrate Na₂CO₃·10H₂O (**washing soda**). It is a **mild base** — too weak to liberate NH₃ from ammonium salts but strong enough to neutralise acids and precipitate metal carbonates. Its reactions with CO₂, SO₂, water and metal salts are the topic's checklist.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Properties - White crystalline decahydrate (washing soda); effloresces on exposure — loses 9 H₂O to become the monohydrate powder. Anhydrous Na₂CO₃ mp 851 °C. - Hydrolysis makes its solutions **mildly basic**: CO₃²⁻ + H₂O ⇌ HCO₃⁻ + OH⁻ (pH ~11 for 0.1 M).…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: SO2 product = Na2SO3 (+CO2), never sulphate. NH4+ test: NaOH yes, Na2CO3 no. Efflorescent = loses water (10H2O -> 1H2O). pH ladder: NaOH ~13, Na2CO3 ~11, NaHCO3 ~8.3.

rows.text: **NEB-style (3m): Describe the action of sodium carbonate on (i) carbon dioxide, (ii) sulphur dioxide, (iii) calcium chloride solution, with equations.** — **(i) CO₂:** in aqueous solution the carbonate absorbs carbon dioxide and water to form the **bicarbonate**: Na₂CO₃ + CO₂ + H₂O → 2NaHCO₃ (the reverse of baking soda's decomposition).…  ·  **NEB-style (2m): Explain why an aqueous solution of sodium carbonate is alkaline although it contains no hydroxide ions in its formula.** — Sodium carbonate is the salt of a strong base (NaOH) and a very weak acid (carbonic acid), so the carbonate ion **hydrolyses water**: CO₃²⁻ + H₂O ⇌ HCO₃⁻ + OH⁻.…

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Carbonate alkalinity is hydrolysis arithmetic: the pH of the solution is set by which acid the anion came from — HCO3- (pKa 10.3) makes CO3^2- a strong grabber of protons, and that is the entire difference between washing soda and baking soda.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Na2CO3: anhydrous soda ash mp 851 C; decahydrate Na2CO3.10H2O washing soda, effloresces -> monohydrate. Mild base by hydrolysis CO3^2- + H2O <-> HCO3- + OH- (pH ~11); NaHCO3 weaker (pH ~8.3). Acids: Na2CO3 + 2HCl -> 2NaCl + H2O + CO2 (brisk effervescence). CO2 + H2O -> 2NaHCO3.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Glass is the biggest consumer of sodium carbonate — about half the world's ~50 Mt annual production goes into the SiO₂–Na₂CO₃ melt; every window pane carries its sodium.

Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 Why Na₂CO₃ is basic but NaHCO₃ is weaker - The carbonate ion is the conjugate base of a very weak acid (HCO₃⁻, pKa₂ ≈ 10.3), so it grabs a proton from water: CO₃²⁻ + H₂O ⇌ HCO₃⁻ + OH⁻. The bicarbonate ion is the conjugate base of a *stronger* acid (H₂CO₃, pKa₁ ≈ 6.4), so its hydrolysis is weaker — pH ~8.3.…  ·  ## 5. Common Confusions **Na₂CO₃ + SO₂ gives Na₂SO₃, not sulphate:** sulphur dioxide is the +4 anhydride — no oxygen is added; oxidation to sulphate would need O₂/oxidant.  ·  **Efflorescence is not deliquescence:** the decahydrate *loses* water to air (efflorescent); NaOH *gains* water (deliquescent). Opposite directions, both about vapour pressure.
